consequence.statement: API endpoints are scheduled for removal; operators using deprecated endpoints should plan migration to replacements.

original.statement: API endpoints are deprecated and scheduled for removal in a future release.

consequence.statement: The Loki 3.0 release notes list some API endpoints as deprecated. They are not removed in this release, so nothing fails yet. The release notes do not name the endpoints or any replacements.
consequence.remediation: Check the deprecated-endpoints list in the Loki API reference and plan to stop using any deprecated endpoints you call.

corrected.statement: Loki 3.0 release notes list API endpoint deprecations under Deprecations; the deprecated endpoints keep working in 3.0 but are deprecated. Operators should review their use of them.

decision.reason: [ev-3401df3ccc78] lists "API endpoint deprecations" under the 3.0 Deprecations section, next to other deprecations [ev-ef5cca6f9d3b][ev-d76b5a54d0e6]. That supports the kind "deprecation" (review): the endpoints are deprecated, not removed, in this release. The proposed statement goes further than the evidence by saying replacements exist to migrate to. The excerpt is only a link and names no endpoints, replacements or removal timeline, so I have narrowed the statement to what the evidence says.
